title: Review pack: AgentCore Runtime × Redshift × IAM Identity Center (OBO / 2LO / 3LO)
intro: All resources were deployed by the numbered, idempotent scripts in `infra/` (01 → 13), in this order. For every step this pack lists what the script created, an AWS console screenshot per resource (exact URL and capture time shown under each image; open the URL to validate), and read-only verification commands run when the pack was built, with the expected pattern and the actual output. Functional test results (OBO 16/16 matrix, 2LO/3LO 18/18) are in `RUNBOOK.md` and `tests/results-*.txt`.

steps.title: Runtime VPC with a fixed egress IP (ap-southeast-1)
steps.purpose: Private subnets for the AgentCore Runtime ENIs; all egress goes through one NAT gateway with an Elastic IP, so Redshift can allowlist exactly one IP for the agent.

verify.name: runtime SG has no inbound rules

steps.title: Cognito user pool (end-user IdP, admin-only users)
steps.purpose: Cognito issues the users' ID tokens (JWT). Users are admin-created with emails that mirror IAM Identity Center users; self sign-up is disabled because email is the identity mapping key.

steps.title: IdC Trusted Token Issuer + Redshift IdC application
steps.purpose: The TTI tells IAM Identity Center to trust JWTs signed by the Cognito pool and maps the `email` claim to the IdC user's `emails.value`. The Redshift IdC application (namespace AWSIDC) accepts that TTI for audience = the OBO client.

verify.name: Redshift IdC app trusts the TTI for the OBO audience

steps.title: Redshift cluster, network-restricted (ap-east-1)
steps.purpose: ra3.large single node attached to the IdC application. Port 5439 is open only to the operator workstation egress IPs and the runtime NAT EIP; no egress rules. The admin password is managed by Secrets Manager.

verify.name: SG ingress = 3 × /32 on 5439, no 0.0.0.0/0
verify.cmd: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --region $IDC_REGION --group-ids $RS_SG_ID --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissions[].IpRanges[].CidrIp' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | sort | tr '\n' ' '

steps.title: Seed data + grants to IdC group roles (SQL)
steps.purpose: Tables in `dev` (sales.orders, marketing.campaigns, risk.credit_limits), roles `AWSIDC:<group>`, table/column grants and RLS. No console page; verified with the Redshift Data API (read-only SELECT).

verify.name: IdC group roles exist
RLS enabled on sales.orders

steps.title: OBO runtime execution role (no Redshift permissions)
steps.purpose: Role assumed by the OBO runtime. It can call Bedrock, write logs, use its workload identity, and (added in step 7) exchange tokens at one IdC application. It has no `redshift:*` permission.

verify.name: no redshift actions in any inline policy
verify.cmd: for p in $(aws iam list-role-policies --role-name rsidc-agent-runtime-role --query PolicyNames --output text); do aws iam get-role-policy --role-name rsidc-agent-runtime-role --policy-name $p --query PolicyDocument; done | grep -c 'redshift:' ; true

steps.title: IdC customer-managed app for the agent's token exchange
steps.purpose: `rsidc-data-agent` has a jwt-bearer grant trusting the Cognito TTI (audience = OBO client), scope `redshift:connect`, required group assignment, and an ActorPolicy that allows only the OBO runtime role and explicitly denies every other principal.

verify.name: jwt-bearer grant → Cognito TTI, OBO audience
ActorPolicy: Allow runtime role + Deny everyone else

steps.title: OBO data agent on AgentCore Runtime
steps.purpose: Direct code deploy (zip in S3). VPC mode in the private subnets, JWT inbound auth (Cognito discovery, audience = OBO client), Authorization header forwarded to the agent.

verify.name: runtime READY, VPC, JWT audience, header allowlist

steps.title: Cognito OAuth clients for 2LO / 3LO (same pool)
steps.purpose: Managed login domain (v2), resource server `rsidc-reports/read`, a confidential client_credentials client (2LO) and a confidential authorization-code client (3LO). The OBO client is unchanged here.

steps.title: AgentCore Identity credential providers
steps.purpose: Two CustomOauth2 providers backed by Cognito discovery: `rsidc-2lo-cognito` (M2M) and `rsidc-3lo-cognito` (user federation). Client secrets are held by AgentCore Identity (Secrets Manager, never printed).

steps.title: 2LO downstream: Gateway → Lambda → Redshift service user
steps.purpose: DB user `svc_reporting`; Lambda that queries Redshift through the Data API as that user; AgentCore Gateway (MCP) whose JWT authorizer accepts only the 2LO client; target `reporting` invoked with the Gateway IAM role.

verify.name: Lambda may impersonate only svc_reporting
verify.cmd: aws iam get-role-policy --role-name rsidc-reporting-lambda-role --policy-name reporting --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[0].Resource' --output text

steps.title: Separate OAuth agent runtime (2LO / 3LO)
steps.purpose: `rsidc_oauth_agent` with its own role. The role grants `GetResourceOauth2Token` on the token vault, both credential providers and its own workload identity, plus read access to the two provider client secrets; this is what lets the runtime use `rsidc-2lo-cognito` / `rsidc-3lo-cognito`. The workload identity allowlists the 3LO return URLs.

verify.name: role grants GetResourceOauth2Token on the 2LO provider
verify.cmd: aws iam get-role-policy --role-name rsidc-oauth-runtime-role --policy-name oauth-runtime --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[?Sid==`OutboundOAuthTokens`].Resource[]' --output text

verify.name: runtime READY with provider names in env

steps.title: Browser sign-in for the local web GUIs
steps.purpose: Adds managed login (authorization code + PKCE) and the callbacks `http://localhost:8080/callback` (OBO GUI) and `http://localhost:8081/callback` (2LO/3LO GUI) to the existing OBO client. Only OAuth fields change; the audience stays the same.

verify.name: code flow + both localhost callbacks; password auth kept

findings: OBO enforces IdC per-user access in Redshift (16/16 matrix). The runtime role has no Redshift permission; every session runs as `AWSIDC:<user>`.
External JWTs are single-use at IdC; the agent exchanges once per sign-in (history/001).
An Allow-only IdC app ActorPolicy did not stop same-account admins; fixed with an explicit Deny (history/002, verified in step 7).
2LO bypasses per-user controls by design: every user, including one with no grants, saw all rows with PII via `svc_reporting` (step 11).

3LO: Token Vault isolation and session binding work; a shared IdP browser session can store another user's token, mitigated by the agent identity guard (history/003). `prompt=login` via customParameters stored no token (observed).

Console pitfalls (recorded in the aws-deploy-evidence skill): IdC tabs don't change the URL; Gateway deep links redirect to home; IAM inline policies must be expanded; full-page shots can hide a field behind the sticky footer.
teardown: `infra/run.sh ./infra/99-teardown.sh` (asks for `delete rsidc`) deletes everything above in reverse order, including the Redshift cluster **without a final snapshot**. The pre-existing IAM Identity Center instance, users and groups are not touched. Running cost while deployed ≈ USD 0.72/hour.
